items.title: Breaking: Victorian police reveal they 'strongly believe' fugitive Dezi Freeman is dead
items.description: Victoria Police will spend five days scouring a remote section of Mount Buffalo National Park in the state's north-east as part of a renewed search for fugitive Dezi Freeman.

items.title: The economy should be the focus but Coalition incompetence is a gift to Labor
items.description: The trip to the tennis is a sign of the PM's own sense of confidence. It's a move that is only made by a man who clearly has his mojo back.

items.title: Live: Albanese likens 'bizarre' Liberal, National infighting to reality TV
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has likened the leadership troubles engulfing the Liberal and National parties to a reality television show. Follow live.

items.title: 'I accepted my fate': They shielded kids from bullets, preparing for the worst
items.description: Survivors, grieving family members and those who ran towards danger describe, in their own words, what they witnessed as the Bondi attack unfolded.

items.title: Grandparents left in disbelief and frustrated by family law system
items.description: Many grandparents are parting with hundreds of thousands of dollars to help support their adult children through family law matters, in turn impacting their own financial security in retirement.

items.title: Live: ASX down as gold miners tumble on precious metals rout
items.description: The local stock market is in the red, led by hefty falls for gold miners as precious metals continue to react negatively to the announcement of the US Fed chair. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Home prices rise as first-time buyers, investors see 'intense competition'
items.description: Property prices rose across the country in January, but analysts expect the pace of growth to slow as forecast rate hikes put off prospective buyers.

items.title: Further charges unlikely in Epstein case, top prosecutor says
items.description: Deputy Attorney-General Todd Blanche says the existence of "horrible photographs" and troubling emails in the latest cache of released files does not necessarily mean prosecutions can go ahead.

items.title: Iran's supreme leader warns US attack would start 'regional war'
items.description: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei issues his most direct threat yet following the deployment of US warships to the Arabian Sea.

items.title: Live: Grammys 2026: Aussie artist already on the winners' board as ceremony begins
items.description: The biggest music stars have started to arrive at the 68th Grammy Awards, with top nominees including Kendrick Lamar, Lady Gaga and Bad Bunny.

items.title: 'Punished by association': Families trapped indefinitely inside ICE detention
items.description: The Trump administration's rapid expansion of ICE detention centres has led to inhumane conditions, record deaths and allegations of abuse, civil rights watchdogs warn.

items.title: Liberals expect leadership spill against Ley as early as next week
items.description: Leadership speculation has engulfed both the Liberal and National parties since the minor party walked away from the Coalition agreement two weeks ago.

items.title: The moment Djokovic knew Alcaraz was 'destined for great things'
items.description: Despite the hollow feeling of defeat, 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic heaps praise on Carlos Alcaraz following the Spaniard's history-making Australian Open victory.

items.title: Aussie Olympic preparations continue after COVID-19 positive tests
items.description: Australia's Winter Olympics preparations will continue with minimal fuss in northern Italy despite two members of staff testing positive for COVID-19.

items.title: 'No time to think': How four teens rescued two swimmers
items.description: Angus Mayes has been caught in a rip before — so he knew how serious a situation it was when he heard screaming at a beach.

items.title: The 'very simple' ways a dog knows how you're feeling
items.description: Your dog is constantly reading you and using it to their advantage. These are the cues they use to foresee your next move.

items.title: Matildas trio help Arsenal to become first-ever club world champions
items.description: Arsenal have become the first women's world soccer champions, with Matildas star Caitlin Foord clinching the title for the Gunners in extra time.

items.title: Premiership-winning player sues AFL over 'catastrophic' concussion
items.description: Nightcliff Tigers dual-premiership player Trent Melville is suing the AFL in the NT Supreme Court after suffering "catastrophic injuries" in a head clash with another player in 2022.

items.title: Hundreds of rescued baby swans nursed back to health
items.description: Wildlife volunteers in WA's South West are urging people to get involved in caring for hundreds of baby swans found abandoned over summer.

items.title: The 'apocalyptic Christian cult' attempting to convert pastors
items.description: A former member of cult-like religious group Shincheonji says the group targets pastors around the world in an attempt to boost membership by recruiting entire congregations.

items.title: Police hunt teen suspect over alleged park toilet sexual assault
items.description: Police say a teenage boy was sexually assaulted at a toilet block in Adelaide's south on Saturday by another young male who had asked for help to "look for his lost mobile phone".

items.title: Dinosaur footprint found in Brisbane quarry more than 60 years ago identified
items.description: A fossilised dinosaur footprint that lived in a professor's personal collection for more than six decades has been identified.

items.title: Aussies suffer record loss, Pakistan boycotts World Cup clash with India
items.description: Australia slumps to a 3-0 T20 series defeat in Pakistan, leading into this month's World Cup.

items.title: Small towns fight to keep their schools open amid low enrolments
items.description: As the gates shut at five tiny schools across regional New South Wales, residents fear the loss will be felt far beyond the classroom.

items.title: Winds up to 80km/h to break heatwave, but Qld north floods could last weeks
items.description: Flooding in north Queensland could last for several more weeks, and while the heatwave that has blanketed parts of the state comes to an end, it will be replaced by storms and severe winds.
